source: the raw records of the runners of GitHub, judged again with the catalog after the calibration of the propagation

cells.name: iptables, callers learn that a prober fails while the pod can serve: endpoints only

prediction.text: The algebra predicts a false removal: the replica can serve, but it leaves the EndpointSlice and the rules of each node. The band is 12 s to 24.105 s after the fault. The readiness check of the target fails for the hold (30 s), but its route still serves. Its latch trips 8 s–18 s after the fault. Then the controller of the service is not ready, thus the service refuses each request with a 503. The kubelet and the propagation (CAL.T07.iptables: median 0.059 s, 33 times) remove the target 12 s–24.105 s after the fault: a false removal. Each connection to the target stays open, and the rules select a backend only for a new connection. Thus each request on those connections fails from the trip until the readiness of the service recovers, up to 6.16 s after the heal. 7–17 of the 24 connections are on the target, thus about 525–2992 requests fail.

cells.why: Each of the 3 counted runs agrees with the prediction. The median is 16.855 s. The counted runs measured 13.839 s to 19.751 s.

cells.name: iptables, callers learn that a prober fails while the pod can serve: in band (lame duck)

Each refusal closes its connection, and the next request opens a new connection one turn (0.16 s) later. A chain of picks of the target ends at the first pick of the other replica. Each pick goes to the target at random, thus the failures of the 24 connections are negative binomial: 12–39 in 95 % of the runs. A chain longer than 14 picks has a chance of 0.001 at the most.
